The future of BioWare's franchise remains uncertain

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

A BioWare veteran who most recently worked on Mass Effect 5 doesn't have much hope EA will sell the IP. In fact, they reckon it'll be a "miracle" if we get another RPG, book, or comic.

News of BioWare's closure and the cancellation of Mass Effect 5 (Universe, as it was called) came following the recent EA buyout – news that hasn't exactly gone over well with fans eagerly awaiting the studio's now-dead RPG.

In fact, it spurred an entire movement and the Save Mass Effect petition, which garnered thousands of signatures. Heck, fans even gathered outside of EA offices to protest the death of what might have been the biggest Mass Effect to date – but in terms of any concrete word on a revival of sorts… Well, there's been nothing. And, sadly, it's likely to stay that way, as former Mass Effect Universe developer and Annihilation author Cat Valente admits.

She implies as much over on Reddit, telling a fan that she's not sure another publisher or company will swoop in and somehow buy BioWare in hopes of saving the Mass Effect team, or that the franchise will see a comeback: "I want to be wrong, I truly do. But because I am a gamer, despite what the hordes of X would say, I've been burned by EA before and I don't really believe in my heart they'll let it go."

Valente continues, explaining that any offshoot of the series would be nothing short of "a miracle" – should it ever happen in the first place – and will likely have to do with the Mass Effect TV show. "If they allow books or comics or RPGs or something of the sort, that will be a miracle, but probably be connected to the show (if that happens, it's been in development hell forever) than anything I ever worked on or even the trilogy," she says.

None of this means Valente doesn't want more Mass Effect. "I want to believe! I cried seeing that billboard in Times Square. I think the last 10 years have made me into a cynic when it comes to enshittification, and because I poured years of my finite mortal life into this, it hurts too much to hope, so I prepare myself for disappointment," she states. Not to mention that, uh, if anything did come to fruition, it might not be… ideal.

It would never be from the BioWare fans grew to love over three decades. "Especially since, if it did get a new home, it almost certainly wouldn't include much or anything of what I (or our team) did," as Valente describes. "A new owner would want to put their own spin on it and start from scratch – maybe people would be hired back, maybe not, but it's hard to see a way that what I worked on would be what a totally different studio felt beholden to."

Sign up to our Switch 2 Spotlight newsletter to make sure you get the very latest news on Nintendo's new console and its games every week

She doesn't want the community to give up hope, though: "Don't stop fighting, don't stop believing, hold the line, prove me wrong." Unfortunately, however, Valente isn't the only one who feels… uncertain. Another ex-dev said "EA never actually sells anything" and we shouldn't expect a rekindling of Universe as "they just shut things down and sit on their licenses." You know, like American McGee's Alice.

Much like Valente and other past devs, I wouldn't hold my breath – but I also agree that fans shouldn't abandon all hope, as every desired outcome has to start somewhere. It's evident that Mass Effect isn't going down without stirring a storm, at least.

Mass Effect Universe would "clean up" Mass Effect 3's endings "in a way that wouldn't piss everyone off," writer says

After spending years with her head in various fantastical realms' clouds, Anna studied English Literature and then Medieval History at the University of Edinburgh, going on to specialize in narrative design and video game journalism as a writer. She has written for various publications since her postgraduate studies, including Dexerto, Fanbyte, GameSpot, IGN, PCGamesN, and more. When she's not frantically trying to form words into coherent sentences, she's probably daydreaming about becoming a fairy druid and befriending every animal or she's spending a thousand (more) hours traversing the Underdark in Baldur's Gate 3. If you spot her away from her PC, you'll always find Anna with a fantasy book, a handheld video game console of some sort, and a Tamagotchi or two on hand.

#3692. Valve push on with their Steam improvements by revamping the Community Market home page and adding a watchlist to it so you're bookmarks will be a lot lighter

Another day, another Steam update! Earlier this year, Valve made some tweaks to Steam's Community Market as part of their ongoing widening of the digital storefront. The maybe Half-Life 3 developer is back with another update for the Community Market, once again bringing some fresh UI/UX bits, as well as some quality of life adjustments that should make it a bit nicer to use.

For starters, there's a new Market home page! "We've rebuilt the Market Home to load faster and present you with the most relevant items from your games," a blog post explains. "Instead of the Popular Items section, which was a small and static slice of millions of items, Trending Items will give you a glimpse into what’s new in the games you’re currently playing. The game links move up to the top spot and are now personalized, so rather than a flat and unchanging list, you get quick access to the items you're most likely to be interested in."

Next up in the update is the addition of a watchlist feature. Before, if you wanted to follow a number of items in the marketplace you'd need to bookmark everything, but now you can just save things to your watchlist; this includes the likes of specific listings, particular item types with any filters you've applied, and even specific searches, again with filters and search text. You can also apply custom names to watchlist entries in case two of them end up looking particularly similar.

There were a few other smaller bits to this update too. You'll find a new section that highlights Steam community items, i.e. trading cards and emotes, from games you've played. If you have anything listed on the marketplace, you can now change the price without having to relist it. There's a list view option while browsing items. And market pages now load faster and are more responsive. A convenient sounding update for the Steam Community Market connoisseur! Which is already live, by the way.

#3691. GTA 6 credits actually include 'Florida Joker', the viral internet personality who once demanded $10 million from Rockstar Games

Lawrence Sullivan, better known to the online world as the 'Florida Joker', is in GTA 6. After accusing Rockstar Games of using his likeness without consent and then demanding a $10m payout, the two parties have seemingly settled their differences.

Grand Theft Auto 6's earliest controversy came from its very first official trailer, when Sullivan alleged one of the teaser's similarly tattooed characters was modeled after him. The former tattoo model, who first went viral because of a mugshot that shared an uncanny resemblance to Batman's Joker, soon called on Rockstar to pay him $2m. His demand quickly shot up to $10m, before he dropped all legal threats and politely asked to officially work with the developer.

Rockstar seems to have relented to that last request - the vast GTA 6 credits include none other than one Lawrence Sullivan, listed under the 'Local Population' cast, alongside dozens of other names.

GTA 6 players wasted no time, and quickly found the suspect first teased way back in that original 2023 trailer. In its quest to parody all parts of modern life under capitalism, GTA 6 lets you doomscroll through a social media app called Snapmatic, which flings an endless number of short-form clips and thirst traps at you. If you're lucky enough, or if you scroll for long enough, you'll find a video of Sullivan's in-game counterpart beating up a fake lookalike. He certainly sounds like Sullivan, too.

"Two years y'all been talking crazy about me," he wrote under a recent Instagram post. "Who got the last laugh now?!"

The GTA 6 credits were illuminating for other reasons, too. We finally know who voices the game's loveable duo, Jason and Lucia, for one. All 34 of the infamously fired Rockstar workers also appear in GTA 6's credits. The controversial move eventually led to accusations of union busting on Rockstar's part, which is currently being investigated as part of an employment tribunal in Scotland.

Rockstar brought weather back to Leonida.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

In my first 30 hours of Grand Theft Auto 6, I think I saw it rain once. And that was during a particularly gloomy main story mission where it felt like it was intentionally flipped on and not a serendipitous moment created by the game's weather system.

I was not alone in wondering what was up with the weather in Leonida. GTA 6 players have been confused by the lack of rain and fog since day one, especially after Rockstar boasted about the kind of storms and hurricanes it can create to Game Informer in September.

Apparently, the questioning was justified: The weather system was broken and should now be fixed in a new patch that went out today.

"Fixed an issue that resulted in weather not changing for extended periods," the patch notes say, confirming that, while some players witnessed changes in weather, it was not properly happening at the rate it was intended.

You don't partner with The Weather Channel to post exclusive pre-release screenshots of your game if the forecast is mostly sunny and not actually representative of Florida, the state with the most unpredictable weather in the US. GTA 6 has realistically detailed radio towers that left a TikTok guy who's worked on them in real life gobsmacked. It would've been bizarre if Rockstar neglected to put that kind of effort into a system normies like me would notice within a few hours.

The sun's reign is over and all the other meteorological conditions can take the spotlight. As someone who takes their time doing all the silly little daily routines in Jason and Lucia's life and abiding by traffic laws for the vibes, I'm excited to see how much the weather affects the mood. I'll just have to remember to be a little more discerning when chasing down one of GTA 6's cars to make sure I don't absolutely ruin the interior from a surprise storm.

Marvel Rivals is officially getting its first Lego set, with a Lego Jeff the Land Shark model swimming out of the screen and onto shelves at the beginning of next year.

Due to land on January 1, 2027, this model is made up of just under 500 pieces and is a mid-size figure – it's around 5 inches high and 8.5 inches long. Rather than being a static display, though, it mimics some of the best Lego sets and is much more interactive than that. The mouth, legs, tongue, and tail of Lego Jeff the Land Shark all move, letting you set up the Marvel Rivals character however you want.

Like so many Marvel kits, this one straddles the line between playset and display piece. It's rated for ages 12+ and seems sturdy enough for younger fans to have a lot of fun with, but is also highly posable so collectors can show off Jeff at his best.UK: £44.99 at Lego

If you've been following the week's Lego news, you'll know that this isn't the first we've seen of the adorable critter; the model was leaked ahead of time, and it divided fans. From initial reactions, it feels as though the community was split down the middle. Some felt it was an adorable rendition of Jeff and were happy to see it, while others really didn't like the design.

Now that we've got official promo shots, I think Lego Jeff the Land Shark comes off much better than it did in leaks. It's true that the final product doesn't capture how squidgy and rotund the character looks in-game, but that was always going to be a tall order – Lego is obviously angular by design so doesn't lend itself to soft, circular shapes unless you're building something massive. As such, I think the team has done a great job considering the scale of the model.

#3687. "That philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6": CD Projekt Red are staying the course on The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2 after Rockstar's smash success

"We have certain ambitions when it comes to [The Witcher 4 and] Cyberpunk 2"

For publicly traded game developers, there is surely one question, with all manner of variations, that will surely be coming up again and again over the next few months: what impact will GTA 6 have on your games? CD Projekt Red were subjected to such questioning in their latest earnings call, part of which was related to sales figures of The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077, that boring kind of thing. But CEO Michal Nowakowski did also respond to a comment about how GTA 6 may affect the development of The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2.

"We have certain ambitions when it comes to [The Witcher 4 and] Cyberpunk 2, they have not changed when it comes to GTA 6," Nowakowski quite plainly explains in response to a question about how the biggest game of the year may influence budget or design, already sounding just that little bit exasperated over the questions related to Rockstar's latest. "If anything happened as a result of GTA 6, it's always great to see games like that because they show you how much cool stuff can be done. That's for sure an inspiration in many ways for our developers. In terms of the budget, I gave a response [in an interview at] Gamescom; games The Witcher or Cyberpunk 2, although they are not GTA, are not budget-driven developments."

Nowakowski goes on to clarify that he doesn't mean this in the sense of not caring about budgets, or that they have infinite money, but noted that you "cannot make games," with solely that focus. "They are ambition-driven developments and money is important, the budgets are not indefinite, that's not what we're saying. And honestly, that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6." This is obviously kind of a non-answer in one sense, but I think it does point to how GTA 6 is going to create some uncomfortable expectations for many triple-A devs when next to none of them will have Rockstar money to fulfill them.

In any case, obviously the next big thing for CD Projekt Red is The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion. Still no release date attached to that one, though it's currently expected to release sometime in 2027 next year. The Witcher 4 is then slated for release not long after that in 2028, but in this day and age, I'm sure a delay would be an incredibly safe bet to make.

#3686. After taking seven years to make Persona 6 and four years to make Persona 5, Atlus promises future games will come quicker

"People won't have to wait as long for the next game as they have previously."

Persona 6 is still slowly chugging in the background, but developer Atlus is promising that future games in its beloved RPG series won't take quite as long as they used to.

There was a four year gap between 2012's Persona 4 Golden and the original Persona 5, and it's already been seven years since the expanded Persona 5 Royal first dropped. Despite the sometimes agonising wait filled with countless spin-offs and collaborations with live service games, we've only seen a vague teaser trailer for the next proper Persona.

P-Studio general producer Kazuhisa Wada recently assured folks that the pattern wouldn't repeat again. "Persona 6 is not the end," he said in a Sega Samania interview translated by GamesRadar. "We have been working to make sure that people won't have to wait as long for the next game as they have previously. In order for Persona to grow as an IP, we consider how to live up to people's expectations in terms of creativity and development every day."

Wada doesn't go into any more detail about how Atlus plans to release Persona games quicker. Is the next mainline game already in development alongside Persona 6, or is Atlus just streamlining how it makes games? Either way, the studio seems to have abandoned its divisive habit of returning to and improving its games after a few years - P3 Portable, P4 Golden, P5 Royal. I imagine that'll cut down on wait times, at least somewhat.

"Large-scale RPGs like the Persona series take five years or more to develop," he added. "So there can be a long time between numbered entries."

As for Persona 6 itself, Wada unsurprisingly "can't say much" about the much-hyped, high-schooling, demon-punching game. "But we want our games to demonstrate all of the hard work we've put in. With that in mind, we are creating something better than anything we've made before, and that is hugely satisfying."

We don't know much about Atlus' occult sequel, officially, but a massive information leak earlier in the year revealed a full achievement list for Persona 6 and a bunch of other unreleased games, including Kingdom Hearts 4 and an unannounced Sea of Thieves project. Be wary of online spoilers, then.

It's been a big week for videogames—or rather, videogame. Grand Theft Auto 6 is enjoying what may very well be the single greatest media launch in history, securing over $3.7 billion in launch sales. But as Rockstar enjoys its acclaim, other developers—like Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski—are professing some anxiety about releasing their own games in a post-GTA 6 world.

"GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression is real. Probably the single greatest artistic achievement in history, I mean it. Scale, density, coherence, thoughtfulness of it all, just a technological and creative miracle," Sarzynski said on Bluesky over the weekend, joking that "Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled."

That news came as a surprise to Cyberpunk 2 lead writer Anna Megill, who replied with a baffled "But wait—"

Sarzynski was, of course, just goofing. But I'm sympathetic to any game dev who might be feeling an amount of apprehension about being measured against GTA 6's success, particularly when there's a genre overlap.

In Cyberpunk 2's case, however, CD Projekt is very much in its own lane: Cyberpunk is a different thematic setting, with entirely different systems and design goals. I'd hope that any reasonable person would think comparing the two is like comparing apples and oranges—particularly when the oranges reportedly had a production budget upwards of $1 billion.

In a follow-up post, Sarzynski acknowledged that each project is doing its own thing, while noting that GTA 6's example will benefit other game developers by serving as a source of creative inspiration.

"Seriously though, I think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor," he said. "GTA is impressive in a way all great art is: It expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed."

Hope you've been training your grip strength

The beauty of stepping into a digital world is that it allows me to accomplish things I couldn't possibly dream of doing in the real one, like, say, climbing anything that's higher than your average step ladder. White Knuckle is one such game that's all about playing around with uncomfortable heights, and a new update for the early access roguelike went live this week introducing a new, hostile environment: The Core.

The sixth region to be added to the game, and the "penultimate challenge," implying that there's just one more area to come after this one, The Core takes you to Habitation Blue's reactor sector. "Use everything you have available to fight through the now Mass-controlled Superstructure Automated Processing System (SAPS) and her array of mechanized defenses," explains a Steam news post. "The Core is the sterile power station of the Superstructure, a massive network of coolant lines, offices, catwalks, and more, all of which is highly secured by an army of turrets, drones, and androids. Even without the Mass hot on your tail it would not be easy to escape."

There are a few new subregions to be found too, of course, but more importantly a new major artifact. It's called The Scissors, and with it you cut off your hands ("yes, really") to "gain a spectral form that increases your reach, hand stamina, and damage," while using the artifact. You can also throw the scissors like a boomerang to hurt enemies from afar, and "killing enemies also counts as eating if using Survival Mode binding, or the perks Conditioned Polyphagia & Unstoppable Conviction."

Beyond this there's a selection of new weapons, like the piton crossbow which shoots "pitons at range, to set up routes and to deal extreme damage." The pulse pump is a new trinket that introduces a chargeable mid-air jump. There's new perks like one called nest egg, where you gain a "second major artifact at the start of the Nest, at the cost of halving all roach deposits in your run." Previous regions have also received some new room tiles, and there's a few fresh cosmetics to pick up too. There's some secret thing to find in this update as well, "but you'll need to play to find out…" Hop to it, I guess!

#3682. GTA 6 is officially the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-sale copies and a bonkers $3.79 billion in its first day

"We are incredibly humbled by the response."

Surprise, surprise - GTA 6 is officially the biggest entertainment launch of all time, surpassing its predecessor's 13-year-long record and the already optimistic analyst estimates.

Rockstar Games today confirmed that its cultural juggernaut sold a staggering 32.5 million pre-release copies across PS5 and Xbox Series X/S before its official worldwide launch on the 19th of November. By the end of its first day on sale, GTA 6 managed to rake in a frankly absurd $3.79bn. Not a bad haul.

As Rockstar was quick to brag, the whopping performance means GTA 6 set "a new record for entertainment across any medium" by "becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history."

For context, GTA 5 made around $800m in its opening 24 hours more than a decade ago. That mammoth debut almost looks quaint next to GTA 6's stunning numbers, although it's notable GTA 5 didn't launch immediately in Japan or Brazil - GTA 6 is available in almost every market with access to PlayStation and Xbox consoles.

"It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI," said Rockstar co-founder and company president, Sam Houser, in a recent press release. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn't be more excited to share this moment with you."

Previous estimates guessed that GTA 6 had sold almost 25m copies ($2.5bn in revenue) on day one. It's fair to say the game's staggering performance blew even those sky-high projections out of the water.

Every early indicator pointed to GTA 6's inevitably record-breaking launch. Parent company Take-Two previously said the game was tracking "well above expectations," as the crime fest sold more pre-orders than any other game in PlayStation Store and Xbox Store history.

The only question now is whether GTA 6 can ever outsell GTA 5's mammoth 230m copies, which it reached thanks to a very healthy cadence of GTA Online updates. How high GTA 6 can go will likely depend on its multiplayer offering, though Rockstar hasn't said anything concrete about that just yet.

"A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that," Chris Tapsell gushed in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

Grinding Gear Games knows a thing or three here

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Right now, the devs behind Path of Exile 2 have a right to be confident. They've created a legitimate rival to the Diablo series, through consistent updates and worthwhile changes, fostering a strong community in the process. During a recent presentation, one of the key devs behind the action-RPG spoke on why he believes their approach to livestreams is much better than the rest of the industry.

Jonathan Rogers, technical director at Path of Exile studio Grinding Gear Games, went into the subject while giving a talk at this year's DevGAMM. "I've seen some truly terrible livestreams for game announcements," he says. "Blizzard, I'm looking at you."

At least he's laying his thoughts out plainly. His first point is a simple one: show the game immediately. "Get to the damn gameplay," he states emphatically. "Nobody cares about your life story, nobody cares about the game's history, nobody cares about how you celebrate your audience or anything like that."

I would definitely be on his side for this much. Too often I find myself sitting through a preview event, waiting for when the actual insight into the game I'm waiting for shows up. The rest is often just fluff.

His second point is another critical one: Lead with your best stuff. "The problem I've seen in presentations is they want to have this Steve Jobs, 'One more thing' moment," Rogers explains. "Don't do that. Lead with the best that you've got, show me what that is. It's just going to get people excited. You want people hyped."

Nintendo is the obvious culprit here, to the point we're all on tenterhooks at the end of every Nintendo Direct, waiting for one last reveal or announcement. There's room to use such things sparingly, but it's a cliché by now. Give us the goods up front!

His remaining four points on this subject are: Sell the story of playing; This is a tutorial; Spoil the game; and it's OK to be long. The first refers to how the game feels to play, the second and third are self-explanatory, and the fourth I'd consider more of a spectrum.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

If we're here strictly for a first look reveal, brevity helps to start. Get to the meat of what you want us to see, then save the rest for a post-show stream. But if you know you have a fanbase ready to devour every fine detail, then rinse whatever you have to showcase.

Path of Exile 2 is about to go 1.0, and it has hundreds of thousands of players. This is a team that knows what they're talking about, especially when it comes to what they don't like about official Diablo and World of Warcraft streams.

Path of Exile 2 is "f***ing genius," Baldur's Gate 3 publishing lead says – early access has been so successful "it won't even matter if nobody buys anything" after 1.0's free-to-play shift

#3680. Bitmap Brothers' iconic, robotic RTS game Z is unofficially back thanks to an open source, 3D remake

There can be such a wonderful charm that comes from fan games because the people that make them really are just in it for the love of the (literal) game. They ain't gonna make any money from this thing! So I'm quite tickled by OpenZ, a 3D remake of the 1996 RTS game Z from The Bitmap Brothers that's completely open source (and, thankfully, hand made).

As it currently stands, OpenZ is a one-person operation who's remaking the game to celebrate its 30th anniversary. "This is the faithful 3D remake we always wanted but never got. Every single detail has been meticulously recreated and restored with an almost ridiculous level of attention," explains the game's itch.io page. "OpenZ is completely free and open source. It will never be sold: no donations, no commercial use, ever. All assets are 100% original, and no copyrighted material from the original game is used."

At the moment there's only two levels, though it's sounding like it's the full run of them, described as having been "meticulously restored and polished to an extreme level of detail," with some added improvements thanks to "30 years of RTS game design experience." There's a few new bits to find in this remake too, like new mech and electrobot units.

It sounds like there are bigger plans for the remake overall, presumably for the full game too: "This is only the beginning. Together as a community we can bring Z back to its former glory: more restored classic levels, completely original new levels, new units and maybe even multiplayer." As mentioned, it's completely free to download and play too, so where's the harm in giving it a go!

#3679. GTA 6 features the series' first non-binary character, says actor Jesse James Rose, and players can't hurt them

Grand Theft Auto 6 features the first non-binary character in the series' history, according to actor Jesse James Rose, who plays the role of a museum curator in the game.

"I can FINALLY share that I play the first-ever nonbinary character in the Grand Theft Auto franchise!" Rose wrote on Instagram.

"Absolutely wild to find out THIS was the super-secret game I spent weeks and 17 NDAs filming 3 years ago."

"I shot this back in my they/them days, and everyone on production ensured I was comfortable and gendered correctly," Rose wrote. The project was kept so secret that Rose wasn't told what it was during filming and only recently learned it was GTA 6.

"GTA was one of the most inclusive & caring sets I've ever been on," they added.

A post shared by Jesse James Rose ✨ (@jamesissmiling)

The role was shot entirely through motion capture, which meant wearing "a unitard made of dots every day". Rose also says steps were taken to protect the character in-game: "To mitigate anti-trans violence, I was assured that players would not be able to inflict violence against my character."

A whole day of the shoot was spent scanning Rose's face, including hours of pulling different expressions. At one point Rose couldn't move a particular muscle, and worried the scan had been ruined, but the director was thrilled.

"That right there is exactly why we'll never use AI," he said, according to Rose. "A computer could never come up with the face you just made."

"Remember, in a world consumed with Generative AI, the largest video game in history chose human labour to preserve the integrity of the game," Rose added.

Rose did raise some concerns about pay, though.

"Despite being paid well for my time on set, I'll never see a residual check for my work," Rose wrote, explaining that this is part of SAG’s contract with game developers. As a union leader at one of SAG's sister unions, Rose said there's still "a long way to go to ensure arts workers are fairly compensated for our labour".

Rose also says many other trans people worked on GTA 6, both in front of the camera and behind it. "SO many trans people besides me are featured in GTA VI as other roles, designers, writers, etc... take a note, theatre and TV! We are employable & profitable!!!"

Finally, Rose voiced support for Rockstar's UK staff. "UK-based workers at Rockstar Games are currently voting on whether to unionise, and I sincerely hope their efforts are successful," Rose wrote. "Every arts worker should have a stable job with benefits and fair working conditions protected by a union."

GTA 6 is out now on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It launched on Thursday, although some have been getting in on the action earlier, as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even New Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first."

Following his guilty plea, Arion Kurtaj was given a seven-year sentence but released "on license" with a warning and restrictions to his online activity..

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

A BBC report says Arion Kurtaj, the Grand Theft Auto 6 leaker who was given an indefinite sentence in hospital in 2023 because he kept hacking into things or expressing intent to, has been released with a stern warning not to do it again.

Kurtaj was sentenced to seven years in prison, according to the report, but was released on license—similar to parole in North America—the same day, with his hospital stay and time in prison while awaiting retrial credited as time served. He was given a five-year "Serious Crime Prevention Order" restricting his allowable online activity, including bans on using Telegram and Discord.

"Kurtaj knew what he was doing when he carried out these crimes and has finally admitted his involvement," Detective Inspector Mike O'Sullivan of the City of London Police said following Kurtaj's sentencing and release. "We hope this case serves as a lesson that these types of acts will not be tolerated.

"Although cyber crime is borderless, we will seek to utilise the co-operation of partner agencies and international law enforcement to ensure that offenders are brought to justice no matter where they offend from."Kurtaj carried out hacks against multiple companies when he was 16 and 17 years old, including Microsoft, Samsung, Nvidia and UK telecom company BT&EE, and stole millions in cryptocurrency from individuals.

But it was his hack of Rockstar and leak of GTA 6 materials more than a year before it was formally revealed, that earned him notoriety, not least because of how it was carried out: While under police protection in a Travelodge hotel room, using an Amazon Fire Stick and a mobile phone.

A psychiatric assessment determined that Kurtaj had "acute autism," and that he "continued to express the intent to return to cybercrime as soon as possible" while he was in custody. That led to his hospital sentence, but earlier this year he was found fit to stand trial and subsequently pleaded guilty to all charges.

That struck me as odd—why plead guilty to crimes carried out at a time when your mental state was such that a court decided you required multiple years of institutionalization?—but this may be the answer: Kurtaj, now 21, is a free man. The judge on the case told Kurtaj he is "a very talented young man," but also warned him: "Don't let this happen again."

#3677. GTA 6 has a 99 Metascore from critics, but players are review bombing it

Grand Theft Auto 6 might be one of the best-reviewed games of all time, but you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score.

While critics have given Rockstar's latest a Metascore of 99, its user score has dropped to 5.6 out of 10 at the time of writing, which Metacritic classifies as "mixed or average". Of the 54,000+ ratings left, 44 percent are "negative".

The score had previously dropped into the red, but has since recovered a little.

Some negative reviews raise genuine complaints, such as the game's 30FPS cap on console, while others take issue with how much of the story focuses on Jason and Lucia's relationship instead of the crime-spree antics of past games.

"Expectations might've killed this game," states one 0/10 review. "The hype that something otherworldly would come to be flopped. The hyperrealism makes it feel slow, mundane and boring. Its a tecnichal [sic] advancement for sure but for the wrong reasons. Goodlooks zero personality type stuff. Its not as edgy as the rest of the gta games. And thats exactly my problem like is not funny. The game gets carried by its visuals and radio stations. Certain limitations make it feel like not gta and new features make it feel like not gta. In the end it feels like a life simulator and the point of gaming is to escape from reality."

"Genuinely hated almost every minute of this experience," wrote another. "After years of waiting and an absurd amount of hype, GTA VI somehow managed to leave me more frustrated than entertained. The excessive sexual content gets exhausting, and instead of adding anything meaningful to the experience, it often feels like Rockstar is desperately trying to shock its audience.

"The story is painfully disappointing, the writing fails to keep me invested, and I honestly couldn't care less about what happens to most of these **** gameplay isn't doing the game any favours either. Glitches, bugs, annoying inconsistencies, and frustrating moments constantly get in the way of actually enjoying the experience. It's ridiculous that a game of this scale, backed by a studio with Rockstar's resources, can feel this rough. I expected a polished experience, not a glorified debugging ****."

Others point to "woke" and "DEI" agendas.

"A major step down in the writing department compared to previous instalments coupled with the obvious DEI-fication, unfun realism and the resulting player freedom restrictions leave a sour taste in the otherwise detailed gorgeous open world," said one reviewer. Another unhappy player wrote: "Shameful DEI hijacked cuck simulator, the most overrated game of all time and it's not even close."

Rockstar wants you to feel the characters' "highs and lows"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

GTA 6 has been in players' hands for a few days now, and one pretty major narrative has emerged - a dissatisfaction among some groups with the pacing and limited stakes of early missions. Particularly before Lucia leaves prison, the more domestic aspects of Jason's story has been a signficant talking point. But that slower pace was part of Rockstar's plan, as writer Michael Wiafe explained in a pre-release briefing on the game.

"We want players to be emotionally in-step with Jason and Lucia, going through the highs and lows they do," he explains. Rockstar wanted players to feel "the thrills and excitement that come with a rebellious rush to escape from economic desperation," but I think it also wanted them to feel Jason's anxiety about building a life for his family, and Lucia's restlessness throughout Chapter 1 that sees her so desperate to find meaningful work.

Those slower moments, Wiafe explains, are all part of "advancing at a rhythm that doesn't feel too off-beat with the player's own playstyle and choices. Distractions along the way, major or minor, are all welcome," and that means that when you do go off into the open-world to explore at your own pace, coming back to the story shouldn't require "a mental reset each time."

Crucially, Rockstar doesn't want you to feel "an overwhelming sense of having to grind in order to progress the story." Wiafe points out that "there obviously is the option here to grind," but says that "the world is so rich and thought-out," that Rockstar hopes players can "just enjoy existing in it to the point where the experience just feels seamless from start to finish." The story, he says, "is happening to Jason and Lucia; however, players should feel they still have all the agency."

It's that final sentence that's why I chose this as today's Quote of the Day, because I think it's where the disconnect lies. A certain subsection of players don't feel as though they've got that agency, because GTA 6 - far more than other games in the series - wants you to feel the investment in and stakes of its world. To some extent, the disconnect comes from holding on too much to what GTA has been in the past; i.e. a criminal sandbox where chaotic rampages are part of the soul of the game. GTA 6 isn't that game, and I'm not sure Rockstar is that studio anymore. But when some players just want to drive a sports car through a crowded beach, any mission - however optional - that asks them to paint a house or collect flowers for their girlfriend is going to be considered antithetical to what the series is supposed to be about.

Some Grand Theft Auto 6 players on PS5 say the game keeps crashing with error code CE-108255-1, and in some cases, it's stopping them from progressing through the story.

"The game runs perfectly fine for a while. I can complete missions and chapters without any issues, but then it suddenly crashes after around 40 minutes and sends me back to the PS5 home screen", wrote one Reddit user. Rockstar hasn't yet acknowledged the crashes or said whether a patch is on the way, and its own support is sending players with console errors to PlayStation or Xbox directly for help.

The Hunger Games movies are once again back on the big screen, and Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters and crushing at the box office. The book to screen adaptation featured a killer cast, including the legendary Glenn Close as Drusilla Sickle. She and Mckenna Grace's Maysilee Donner had slap off in the prequel film, and had thoughts about which one of them had the better one.

Fans of the Hunger Games franchise (which is streaming with a Hulu subscription) were hyped to see a different side to Panem, especially those who read the Sunrise on the Reaping novel. One memorable moment is when Drusilla and Maysilee got into a slapping match on the train, and during a conversation from ET's Instagram, the two actresses joked about who had the better slap. Close responded with:

The Fatal Attraction actress seems to be tipping her hat to Grace, whose character gave her a big slap after the Capitol escort threw hands first. Maysilee is a character with tons of rage, and seeing her defend herself against Drusilla was the audience's first glimpse into that anger.

Of course, Glenn Close's character doesn't take this lightly. She whips out a riding crop and uses it on Maysilee, resulting in the District 12 tribute having welts all over her arms and face. The Oscar-winning actress spoke about this, mentioning:

Well, I ultimately win because I beat you.

Mckenna Grace is a self-described Hunger Games superfan, who seemed thrilled to be playing Maysilee in Sunrise on the Reaping. During the same clip she spoke about how nervous she was for the slap off with Close, offering:

I also worked it up in my head. I was like 'What if a trip? What if I hit Glenn?' And then I was like 'Wait, what if Glenn is kind of method? What if she actually wants to hit me? But I can't morally slap Glenn Close.'

Talk about pressure. Glenn Close is a celebrated icon of the stage and screen, so one can only imagine how daunting it was for Grace to do this scene. Add in that her iconic co-star is 79 years old, accidentally slapping her for real was the thing of nightmares. Luckily that didn't happen, and the scene went viral before the new Hunger Games prequel was even released.

I loved watching the feud between Maysilee and Drusilla during Sunrise on the Reaping, and wish that we got more of their dynamic. There was a ton of content that was cut from the film to keep it short, so maybe we'll get more of this in deleted scenes. Fingers crossed.

The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters now as part of the 2026 movie release list. Clearly audiences are still invested in Panem, so we'll have to see if/when the franchise continues to expand.

#3672. Phasmophobia's next update lets you ask ghosts to throw things and it's out next week

Phasmophobia's next update, Resonance, arrives on 24th November, bringing a brand-new piece of ghost-hunting kit, more voice commands, and a move to the Unity 6 engine.

The headline addition is dowsing rods, which will help you track down the bone, making them particularly handy on bigger maps like Brownstone High School. As with the rest of the game's equipment, the higher the Tier, the more accurate the reading, and Tier 3 Dowsing Rods will pinpoint the exact floor the Bone is on.

The Sound Sensor is getting an overhaul too, with a reworked interface to help you work out where sounds are coming from. Icons will show whether a sound is ongoing or a one-off, and you'll be able to use the map to identify ghosts by how fast they move.

You'll also be able to ask ghosts to interact with doors and switches, and even throw nearby objects, with a list of usable phrases in the Journal. If you're tired of the same maps, you'll be able to build your own pool of maps to randomise from when picking a contract, and new buttons let you quickly pick small, medium, or large maps.

"We want to ensure every item in our Ghost Hunters' kits can add as much value as possible in investigations," said Daniel Knight, CEO and game director at Kinetic Games.

"Resonance also brings Phasmophobia's move to Unity 6 - while this transition is a technical upgrade first and foremost, it has allowed us to implement major lighting improvements to make the game even more immersive."

Alongside more realistic lighting and better stability, the switch to Unity 6 also brings expanded graphics and quality options, VR Eye Adaptation, and a suite of colour-blindness settings.

Resonance will also fix several prominent bugs, and introduce a conduct warning system that alerts players before they're banned, except in cases of severe violations.

Phasmophobia is also adding Xbox Play Anywhere support, so if you own the Xbox digital edition, you'll be able to play on Xbox Series X/S, PC, and devices like the ROG Ally.

Resonance is a free update and will be available on all platforms.

Phasmophobia is available in Early Access on Steam, PS5, PS VR2, and Xbox Series X/S. It's also coming to Nintendo Switch 2, although we still don't quite know when.

Earlier this month, the Phasmophobia community raised more than $230,000 (around £173,000) for the American Heart Association, more than doubling last year's total.

Earlier this year, Kinetic Games confirmed Phasmophobia's 1.0 launch had slipped from this year into 2027, as the studio said it was prioritising quality over speed following a rocky reception to its Player Character Update. The studio ended up apologising to players for issues with the long-awaited update, admitting it "missed the mark" and "didn't deliver on our promises to you".

While Avalancheâs in-house bruiser is willing to operate outside of the confines of the law, the same cannot be said of her merchandising. According to Chinese media [and caught by Automaton Media], Shanghai police have arrested 13 individuals in connection to a bootleg toy operation, who oddly enough specialized in unlicensed dolls of Final Fantasy 7âs Tifa Lockhart.

Shanghai authorities began their investigation in May of this year. Purchasers of a figure based on Lockhartâs negligee appearance at the Honey Bee Inn were disappointed to discover what they received was not quite as advertised. While resembling the merchandise from Play Arts, Square Enixâs in-house toymaker, closer inspection revealed the goods were made of different material, had more simplistic attire and a lack of poseable articulation points. While some might shy away from flagging the cops about such specific buying habits, enough complaints came in to launch further inquiry.

Police have arrested 13 people accused of selling counterfeit Final Fantasy 7 Tifa Lockhart figures

The Chinese sellers reportedly charged higher prices by including extra faces, hands, and accessories not found with the official figures pic.twitter.com/AE1IyS0wi9

In collaboration with the rights holders, police discovered an online network of unauthorized vendors using group chats and digital marketplaces to circulate the inauthentic merch. The ring of counterfeiters allegedly hired the services of a factory in Guangzhou to produce the goods. Police say the operation generated over 2 million yuan (approximately $300,000 USD) and had been selling the knock-offs since 2024. The 13 arrested had set up a front that even included a customer service rep.

Adding insult to injury, the forgeries were sold at a premium compared to the more inexpensive and legitimate article. Because they were unlicensed, the vendors apparently manufactured additional faces and accessories not sanctioned by Square Enix, though sadly they were left unspecified (letâs imagine itâs that cat sandwich NECAâs Alf came with). It is hardly an isolated incident. Like all recent collection frenzies, demand for upper-scale figurines of video game and anime characters has risen rapidly around the globe. GamesRadar says that this year alone, Shanghai police have arrested more than 140 individuals and confiscated over ten million dollars worth of bootleg play things.

The series is pushing it with the extra 30 minutes.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I have watched enough seasons of Survivor to understand the game and have opinions, but not enough to drop Survivor lore. Therefore, I care about the show. It just doesn’t have some of the same dedication and loyalty from me as other reality TV shows. This may be why 2-hour episodes seem like another one of Survivor’s problems.

The last thing Survivor needs is 2-hour episodes.

From years of watching Big Brother, which you can also do with my Paramount+ subscription, I have seen what happens when a reality TV show has far more time than it needs: it misuses it. I don’t want to endure that with Survivor. It doesn’t need an extra 30 minutes. Nothing good can come out of that. We will likely get more fluff and filler, and things that don’t move the story along. More time doesn’t mean a show will effectively use it. We won’t get a season’s maximum potential with more time.

Additionally, Big Brother and similar shows aren’t the only ones to waste the extra time. Netflix reality TV shows play fast and loose with the runtimes. Sometimes the Netflix reality TV shows benefit from a few extra minutes. Other times it feels excessive and boring. I haven't been convinced any reality TV show needs two-hour episodes.

Survivor has worked out earlier issues with the 90-minute format; it doesn’t need to figure out 2 hours.

In the last few seasons, Survivor made some infuriating, questionable choices, so I don’t trust the show to make the best decisions with 2-hour episodes.

When Paramount+ announced a plan to lean more into reality TV, I expected more reality TV. They have announced a few new shows, but not nearly as many or as promising as expected. They have five TV shows under the Paramount+ banner that they could capitalize on with spin-offs. I will always scream to bring Big Brother: Over the Top and Big Brother: Reindeer Games back, but I am open to other ideas to expand that franchise, along with Survivor, The Amazing Race, The Challenge, and RuPaul’s Drag Race.

Instead of giving Survivor 2 hours, pair it with a new Survivor spin-off show to retain some of those viewers. Additionally, I actually prefer watching Survivor with The Amazing Race or another staple CBS reality TV show. I don’t just want a night of only Survivor. Now could be the perfect time to test out a shorter season of Big Brother with Survivor. Create a mini-Big Brother: All Stars spin-off series that only lasts for 30 days, similar to Survivor's length. This could bring in more viewers for each show.

I will gladly watch a three-hour movie (not gladly, but I will do it), but a TV show is pushing it with 2-hour episodes. If Survivor starts doing that, what’s to stop Big Brother, The Amazing Race, and some other reality TV shows?

I personally would be living a nightmare. We have to start limiting how many contestant packages we must see per episode. Change can be good, but this feels like another unnecessary update to the game and viewing.

Spent most of my life in various parts of Illinois, including attending college in Evanston. I have been a life long lover of pop culture, especially television, turned that passion into writing about all things entertainment related. When I'm not writing about pop culture, I can be found channeling Gordon Ramsay by kicking people out the kitchen.

#3668. Unannounced Nioh 3 Complete Edition has been rated in Korea

A rating for the unannounced Nioh 3 Complete Edition has popped up on Korea's Game Rating and Administration Committee (GRAC).

As Insider Gaming spotted, the board gave Nioh 3 Complete Edition a 19+ rating on 17th November after it was submitted on 2nd November, even though Koei Tecmo hasn't announced a Complete Edition for the game yet.

The listing, translated by machine, describes it as "a compilation of additional content from the dark Sengoku action RPG Nioh 3", and gives the rating for "excessive expression of violence", noting that "red blood and body amputation frequently occur during combat".

The listing also notes an overseas rating, which Insider Gaming says is a 17+ rating from Japan's CERO.

Unlike some rating boards, GRAC publishes its ratings as soon as they're decided, which is why game listings often surface there before they're officially announced.

If Koei Tecmo follows the same pattern as Nioh 2, there may not be long to wait. GRAC's records show Nioh 2 was rated in January 2020, and its Complete Edition followed in November that year. Nioh 3 was rated on 14th November 2025, almost exactly a year ago.

Complete Editions typically includes the base game and all of its DLC. It could even launch alongside Nioh 3's second DLC, Bloody Insurrection, which is due in February 2027. Eurogamer has contacted Koei Tecmo for comment and we'll let you know if/when they come back to us.

Back in April, an update introduced "multiple high-difficulty Battle Scrolls" (side missions), accessible from shrines, the addition of a Stone of Penance item "which increases accessory +Values and rarities in exchange for higher difficulties", and new skills given as rewards for completing the aforementioned high-level Battle Scroll missions.

Eurogamer's review of Nioh 3 called the threequel a new high for the 'masocore' series and "the crucible in which all of Team Ninja's experience has been siphoned into." It's sold over one million copies (and counting) since its 6th February launch.

All the endings (and a couple variations) for GTA 6 we've seen so far.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Obviously, massive spoilers follow for GTA 6 endings!

There are multiple endings to GTA 6, and while we haven't experienced them all personally here at PC Gamer, the gaming community has been sharing them around for anyone curious about what they may have missed.

The ending you get depends on the choices you make during the final GTA 6 story mission, but also depends on how you handled Jason and Lucia's romance and criminal profiles throughout the game, so seeing every version of the ending would mean not just playing the ending multiple times, but having different playthroughs of the game altogether.

There are a couple of endings that I don't consider "different" from each other but do have some differences leading up to them, which I'll explain below. There may also be additional endings we haven't seen yet, so we may update this guide in the future.

In the bridge endings, Jason and Lucia have defeated Mendez and his squad and gotten the hard drive back from Georgio's penthouse and escaped. They drive to Cal's place in Key Lento, but discover he has been compromised. They drive to the bridge, but the cops have set up a roadblock and have the couple trapped. Lucia wants to keep going, but Jason suggests they jump off the bridge and swim for it.

A choice comes up on the screen: "Swim For it" or "No Surrender."

Jason and Lucia try to run the roadblock and are shot to death by cops on the bridge. They die holding hands. In the credits, we see that their son Tomas lives happily with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children.

Jason and Lucia are shot to death by cops on the bridge. They die holding hands. In the credits, their lawyer, Abe, brings the money to Lucia's aunt. Tomas lives happily with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children in a much bigger house than the other No Surrender ending.

Choosing "Swim for it" presents an additional choice. When Jason gets out of the car, Lucia can choose to "Exit" the car with him, or change her mind by not choosing it.

Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it. They both exit the car without holding guns. Lucia jumps, but Jason doesn't jump and is arrested. Lucia signs a deal for immunity while Jason goes to prison. Lucia gets a job in a diner. Lucia takes Tomas to meet Jason in prison, but he can only see his son through a glass divider.

Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it. Jason exits the car with a gun, but Lucia changes her mind and stays in the car. The police open fire and Jason and Lucia are both shot to death. Tomas lives with Lucia's aunt, her husband, and their children.

Jason and Lucia decide to jump off the bridge and swim for it, Jason doesn't jump and is arrested. Two years later, Lucia uses the savings account to get Jason freed from prison. Lucia goes to the prison to pick up Jason. Jason meets Tomas and holds his hand.

If you don't have a strong relationship between Jason and Lucia, there is a different ending location: the base of Georgio's tower. In these endings, the couple never makes it to the bridge. You can also choose to break up the couple, either as Jason or as Lucia, as you begin the mission Protective Custody.

After the tower fight with Georgio's men, police confront the couple at the base of the tower. The police open fire and Jason pushes Lucia down. Jason is shot. Lucia has a choice to "Stay down" or "Defend Jason". She stays down and watches Jason die. Lucia is arrested, signs a deal, and visits Tomas at her aunt's house. Lucia then leaves Tomas with her aunt, takes out a gun, and continues her life of crime by preparing to rob a diner.

After the tower fight with Georgio's men, police confront them at the base of the tower. The police open fire and Jason pushes Lucia down. Jason is shot. Lucia chooses "Defend Jason" and fights the cops. They die together.

On the way down to ground level at the tower, Jason decides to run. Lucia is arrested and signs the deal, then lives with her aunt and Tomas while working in a diner. One night there's a knock on the door and she finds a bag of cash on the porch. We see Jason driving away with... Rocco the drug-sniffing dog from earlier in the game. Sure, that might as well happen.

How to get this ending (sourced by GamingwithTZ on YouTube):

Jason and Lucia make a deal with Mendez after defeating him. Once they have the hard drive, they're surrounded by cops at the bottom of the tower. Mendez arrives and takes them away in his car, then drives them to the swamp. Later in the credits, we see two skulls in the swamp, side-by-side, with a bullet hole in each.

Note: You may need a specific criminal profile for this ending. I tried to take the deal (as Lucia) in one of my ending playthroughs, but Jason shot Mendez anyway. I had both Jason and Lucia at "Professional" level criminal profiles. This ending was not available to me. Speculation, but this ending may only be available if you don't have "Professional" as your criminal profiles.

There are potentially (and almost certainly) more endings to GTA 6. There are still a few combinations of all the different variables, including your romance level, criminal profile level, amount of money saved, and the choices you make during the final mission, that we haven't seen yet.

We'll update this guide if the community finds more endings.

Chris started playing PC games in the 1980s, started writing about them in the early 2000s, and (finally) started getting paid to write about them in the late 2000s. Following a few years as a regular freelancer, PC Gamer hired him in 2014, probably so he'd stop emailing them asking for more work. Chris has a love-hate relationship with survival games and an unhealthy fascination with the inner lives of NPCs. He's also a fan of offbeat simulation games, mods, and ignoring storylines in RPGs so he can make up his own.

#3666. Binding Of Isaac Update Review-Bombed Over AI-Generated Music In GTA 6 Mode: ‘Woke Up To A Sh*t Show, Obviously I Had No Idea’

AIGTA 6NicalisSoundtrackSteamThe Binding of Isaac: Repentance+

The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ was a free update to the beloved roguelike that arrived on PC in 2024, but launched on console earlier this week in a head-to-head matchup against Grand Theft Auto 6. The marketing stunt may have been a success, but AI-generated music tracks discovered in a special new Vice City mode have turned the launch into a nightmare.

While Repentance+ came to PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and Switch 2 this week, the Steam version of the game also got a free update. “Be sure to get in and play today’s Daily Run for a very special crime-packed surprise. Enter the Basement, and go out in a glorious blaze of bullets and vehicular homicide!” read the patch notes on on Valve’s storefront. Players could enter the seed “V1CE BSMT” into the roguelike before starting their run to launch a GTA-inspired version with special weapons and music.

Earlier today, however, Reddit user ShweetsStuff posted a comprehensive breakdown of the new music tracks alleging they were made with Suno, an AI-based music generation tool. “The new update includes 14 music files for the run; seven full songs, plus some derivatives (intros/outros),” the wrote. The post continued:

Some include Suno metadata with them. You can find this information yourself by just checking the file comment metadata (something common like VLC has tools for this, but here’s ffprobe output of drivingsong1.ogg, for example):

comment : made with suno; created=2026-10-30T17:53:41Z; id=cd5a5b55-bead-4cb9-949d-09ed1f917dce

Other files have this comment scrubbed; they were edited/exported later, but nonetheless there’s the proof.

Please report issues and bugs to the email attached. https://t.co/KHKSqKGsUe

— ð Edmund McMillen ð (@edmundmcmillen) November 21, 2026

“They’ve had how long now to prepare the GTA 6 release Easter egg daily run literally nobody asked for and still ai slopped it? Are you fucking kidding me,” one fan wrote on the Binding of Isaac subreddit. “No shit, itâs 2026. The entire industry is like this. Cutting corners constantly because they know they can get away with it,” wrote another.

Many have blamed Nicalis, the publisher and co-developer of the Repentance+ expansion, in particular. Complaints about ongoing bugs, latency, and quality control issues have seemingly been building for some time. The latest mishap results in a review-bomb of the expansion’s Steam page, which currently sits at an abysmal user rating of just 9 percent positive. “AI generated music in GTA mode; Edmund please take back control of the game,” reads one of the latest Steam reviews. “Not to mention there’s like single digit bug fixes in a year+ long awaited update with no other changes.”

The AI music was news to Edmund McMillen, the game’s creator. “Woke up to a shit show, obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned,” he posted earlier today on X. An emergency update has since gone out to remove the AI-generated music as well as address some other versions with the latest version of the expansion, but Nicalis has yet to take responsibility for the use of AI or explained how it made it into the game.

Steam requires store page disclosures for any content that uses assets generated with the help of AI, which The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+Â did not have, despite the big publicity push around the latest update and it landing on the same day as Rockstar’s open-world blockbuster. “That was [Nicalis’] idea,” McMillen recently told Eurogamer. “‘Wouldn’t it be funny if…?’ I was like, whatever, that’s funny…We’re done, so we’ve got to release this month…It’s a fun experiment.”

#3665. GTA 6 player gets 30-day PSN ban for sharing in-game nudist photo with a friend

A Grand Theft Auto 6 player says they've been hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network social features ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

Posting on Twitter/X on Friday evening, DerrickGott007 said they had "just got a 30-day PSN social features ban" for sending the photo, which they'd taken with the in-game camera, through PlayStation's messaging service, warning other players not to do the same.

"Do not, I repeat do not send any photos taken with the in-game camera, across the PSN messaging network that contain nudity," they wrote. "I just got a 30-day PSN social features ban for sending my friend a photo of the nudist colony in GTA6 that I found."

In a screenshot of the notice, PlayStation Safety says that content sent from the player's account via Message on PlayStation "breached the Code of Conduct", and that their account has been "temporarily suspended from using PlayStation social features for 30 days" due to "pornographic or obscene content". It also warns that "further offenses may result in temporary or permanent suspension from the whole of PlayStation, not just social features".

PlayStation's Code of Conduct asks players not to "share, solicit, access, distribute or store material that is obscene, pornographic or illegal", and says Sony "may take any action as reasonably necessary to protect PlayStation and our players".

DO NOT, I REPEAT DO NOT SEND ANY PHOTOS TAKEN WITH THE IN GAME CAMERA , ACROSS THE PSN MESSAGING NETWORK THAT CONTAIN NUDITY. I JUST GOT A 30 DAY PSN SOCIAL FEATURES BAN FOR SENDING MY FRIEND A PHOTO OF THE NUDIST COLONY IN GTA6 THAT I FOUND. pic.twitter.com/vsoIjmpGrt

Crucially, as Dexerto points out, the code does not make an exception for content taken from games, even ones rated for adults. So if you've snapped anything cheeky in Leonida - say, full-frontal nudity in its nudist resort - you might want to keep it to yourself.

GTA 6 launched on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and while it's one of the best-reviewed games of all time, you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score, as players review bomb it over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

CDPR wants "shorter intervals between the releases" of its games

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

CD Projekt Red knows that there have been long, long waits between each of its games, and the studio is working to change that. In its latest financial results, the company says that its vast array of upcoming titles is part of an effort to make sure fans don't have to wait so long between games in the future.

The studio "normally" takes between "3 to 6 years to produce a game," as it explains in a new consolidated financial statement. Depending on how you want to count, the gap is even bigger than that – it'll be eight years between the launch of Cyberpunk 2077 and the planned 2028 release of The Witcher 4, though we do have the Phantom Liberty and Songs of the Past expansions helping to fill that gap.

CDPR acknowledges that its revenues are "significantly affected" by its release schedule. "Historically, the studio focused on the development of one major production, with conceptual work on the next game starting even before the production and market release of the previous game were completed. At the moment, the CD PROJEKT RED studio is working in parallel on several productions (also in collaboration with external development teams) and supporting products, which is expected to translate into shorter intervals between the releases of subsequent titles in the future."

The list of upcoming CD Projekt Red games shows the beginning of this plan in action, with projects like The Witcher 4, The Witcher 1 remake, Project Hadar, and Cyberpunk 2 all in various stages of development simultaneously. Of course, the true test of this plan will likely be the gap between The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2, the latter of which has not yet entered full production.

"We are making good progress on Cyberpunk 2," Karolina Gnaś, CDPR's VP of strategy and investor relations, says in an earnings conference call. "We are happy with where we are, but it's still too early to give you a specific date and plan on when we'll move into full production."

Gnaś says that the Cyberpunk 2 team will encompass "around 200 developers by the end of this year," and by the end of 2027 that number should be up to "around 320." With The Witcher 4 set to launch in 2028, that sort of ramp up is an encouraging sign that the studio's plan might just work.

"Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled," says the RPG's director after entering a "GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression"

It's a very exciting time in the MCU, as we're less a month away from the next upcoming Marvel movie, Avengers: Doomsday. The movie is a thrilling concept for fans who spent years watching the Marvel movies in order, as it features entire teams of superheroes uniting against Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom. The first Doomsday trailer was exciting, but the latest (and final) one has bombshell moments from Steve Rogers and Cyclops.

What we know about Avengers: Doomsday is limited, thanks to Marvel's tight security. That's why the new trailer (seen above) is so thrilling, as it offers way more of what we'll get when it arrives in December. To start, we get way more context about Steve and Peggy's happy ending after Endgame. While Avengers Endgame: Encore had Loki showing up during their dance, we'll see as they have years together, raising their son into a full-blown teen. That explains how he gets the long hair and beard that we've been seeing in the footage.

Moviegoers are also psyched about seeing the OG stars of the X-Men movies in the shared universe, and we got more thrilling content from the mutants in this trailer. While we've seen them fighting the Avengers, this trailer showed the two teams uniting against Sentinels. What's more, James Marsden's Cyclops even utters the iconic line:

The shot of the heroes assembling is the thing of nerdy dreams, with the X-Men being teleported into the battlefield courtesy of Alan Cumming's Nightcrawler. Seeing the mutants alongside Steve Rogers, Sam Wilson, Thor, and Reed Richards is downright epic, especially since Cyclops said that beloved line that's been uttered in the comics, as well as X-Men '97 (which is streaming with a Disney+ subscription).

There's plenty of new footage in this trailer, including some epic shots of the movie's action. We also got the first look at Hailee Steinfeld's return as Kate Bishop, which the actress/singer confirmed over the weekend. She's seemingly sharing a scene with Kathryn Newton's Cassie Lang, so maybe the Young Avengers will finally be formed during this movie's mysterious runtime. Of course, fans of Hawkeye mostly want to see Kate and Florence Pugh's Yelena reunite given their A+ chemistry in the MCU series.

While we got plenty of new content in this trailer, there are still countless questions about what The Russo Brothers have up their sleeve for the next Avengers movie. There are tons of characters in play, and just about anything is possible in the Multiverse Saga. Unfortunately, we didn't get any footage of Elizabeth Olsen's Scarlet Witch following her return in VisionQuest, but fans think that she's one of the Latverian Witches that are shown.

Our countless questions will be answered when Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December 18th as part of the 2026 movie release list. Since this is seemingly the final trailer, we might not be getting any more footage until its released.

#3662. Over half of all console players active on GTA 6's launch day played it, says Circana

On Grand Theft Auto 6's launch day, more than half of everyone playing on PS5 and Xbox was playing GTA 6.

Citing new data from Circana's Player Engagement Tracker, analyst Mat Piscatella said on Bluesky that 61 percent of US PlayStation 5 players and 56 percent of global Xbox players who were active on 19th November "engaged with Grand Theft Auto 6".

PS5 players averaged 513 minutes in GTA 6 that day, which is over eight and a half hours, while Xbox players averaged 494 minutes, or around eight and a quarter hours.

"Both the DAU [daily active users] and minutes played engagement rates are absolutely bonkers," Piscatella wrote.

For comparison, Fortnite had the second-highest engagement rate that day, with 10 percent of active players across both platforms playing it.

Piscatella also shared the top five games that GTA 6 players had been playing in the two weeks before launch, between 6th and 19th November: Fortnite, Call of Duty, Grand Theft Auto 5 (Remastered), Roblox, and NBA 2K27.

According to Circana's Player Engagement Tracker, Grand Theft Auto VI had a massive launch (surprise!).For players active on November 19th, 61% of US PlayStation 5 and 56% of global Xbox players engaged with Grand Theft Auto VI.PS5 GTA VI players averaged 513 minutes that day, Xbox players 494.

The figures come after Rockstar confirmed that GTA 6 had become the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day.

GTA 6 launched on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, and while it's one of the best-reviewed games of all time, you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score, as players review bomb it over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Just don't share any, uh, spicy in-game screenshots via PSN - we recently learned that a GTA 6 player was hit with a 30-day PlayStation Network ban after sending a friend a photo they took in the game's nudist resort.

Woll will portray Faye, the "mysterious" wife of Kratos and mother of Atreus.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Deborah Ann Woll said she felt "totally unbothered" by the small but vocal subset of gamers who were upset by the upcoming God of War: Laufey, and apparently she meant it—because today Amazon MGM Studios announced that she's going to play the same role in the live-action God of War series coming to Prime.

Just as in God of War: Laufey and its predecessor, God of War: Ragnarok, Woll—best known for playing Karen Page in Marvel's Daredevil, Defenders, and Punisher TV series, as well as a lengthy stint on True Blood as Jessica Hamby—will portray Faye, wife of Kratos and mother of Atreus.

"Faye’s abrupt passing sets in motion the events of God of War," the announcement says. "Along their journey, Kratos and Atreus discover secrets about Faye that make them wonder how well they truly knew her at all."

It's been a bumpy road for the God of War series. It was first reported in 2022, but started over from scratch two years later after the showrunner and executive producers quit. We got our first look at Ryan Hurst as Kratos earlier this year—not very impressive, but we all had the same initial impression of Henry Cavill as Geralt and that worked out well—but then Hurst had to be recast because of an on-set injury; Dave Bautista now has the lead role. Child actors Callum Vinson and Island Austin, who played Atreus and Thrud, were also recast.

God of War: Laufey is set to launch on May 20, 2027, but sadly is a PlayStation 5 exclusive, a state of affairs that seems likely to endure given Sony's recent strategy shift. The God of War live action series on Prime has been ordered for two seasons, but a release target hasn't been announced.
